jobs.title: Licensed Master Social Worker
jobs.description:
Company Description
Parkview Professional Counseling is an established outpatient mental health practice serving individuals and families throughout the Greater Grand Rapids community from its location in Wyoming, Michigan. The practice offers comprehensive behavioral health services delivered by fully licensed clinicians in counseling, social work, and marriage and family therapy. Practitioners benefit from strong operational infrastructure, quality office space, and dedicated administrative support, allowing them to focus on providing client-centered care. Parkview fosters a collaborative, supportive, and faith-informed professional culture that values clinical excellence, professional autonomy, and ethical practice. The organization is committed to maintaining high standards of integrity in service to both clinicians and the community.
Role Description
The Licensed Master Social Worker (LMSW) provides outpatient psychotherapy and clinical social work services to individuals, couples, and families in an on-site setting in Wyoming, MI. This full-time role includes conducting diagnostic assessments, developing treatment plans, and delivering evidence-based interventions aligned with client needs and practice standards. The LMSW maintains timely and accurate clinical documentation, coordinates care with other Parkview clinicians, and collaborates with external providers or community resources when appropriate. The role involves participating in case consultation, contributing to a supportive team environment, and upholding ethical, culturally responsive, and faith-informed practice consistent with Parkview’s values. The LMSW is expected to manage a stable caseload, maintain professional boundaries, and actively engage in ongoing professional development.
Qualifications

Current Michigan LMSW license in good standing and eligibility to practice clinical social work independently.
Demonstrated proficiency in conducting biopsychosocial assessments, formulating diagnoses, and creating evidence-based treatment plans.
Experience providing individual, couple, and family therapy using modalities such as CBT, DBT, solution-focused, or trauma-informed approaches.
Strong skills in clinical documentation, electronic health record (EHR) use, and adherence to legal, ethical, and regulatory standards.
Ability to collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary team and coordinate care with community and medical providers.
Commitment to culturally responsive practice, respect for diverse backgrounds and beliefs, and sensitivity to faith-informed care.
Excellent interpersonal communication, boundary-setting, and crisis intervention skills.
Master’s degree in Social Work from an accredited program; prior outpatient or private practice experience preferred.
Willingness to maintain a full-time on-site schedule and engage in supervision, consultation, and continuing education.

Conducts assessments to identify individual needs.
Develops comprehensive care plan to address objectives and goals as identified during assessment.
Supports member access to appropriate quality and cost effective care and modifies plan(s) as needed.
Coordinates with internal and external resources to meet identified needs of the member in terms of integrated (physical and behavioral) whole person care.

Experience working with specialty populations preferred.
Clinical experience in social work counseling with a broad range of complex psychiatric/substance abuse and/or medical disorders preferred.
Experience working with children in Foster Care or Adoption preferred.

Company Description
Parkview Professional Counseling is an established outpatient mental health practice serving individuals and families throughout the Greater Grand Rapids community from its location in Wyoming, Michigan. The practice offers comprehensive behavioral health services delivered by fully licensed clinicians in counseling, social work, and marriage and family therapy. The LMSW is expected to manage a stable caseload, maintain professional boundaries, and actively engage in ongoing professional development.

Current Michigan LMSW license in good standing and eligibility to practice clinical social work independently.
Demonstrated proficiency in conducting biopsychosocial assessments, formulating diagnoses, and creating evidence-based treatment plans.
Experience providing individual, couple, and family therapy using modalities such as CBT, DBT, solution-focused, or trauma-informed approaches.
Strong skills in clinical documentation, electronic health record (EHR) use, and adherence to legal, ethical, and regulatory standards.
Ability to collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary team and coordinate care with community and medical providers.
Commitment to culturally responsive practice, respect for diverse backgrounds and beliefs, and sensitivity to faith-informed care.
Excellent interpersonal communication, boundary-setting, and crisis intervention skills.
Master’s degree in Social Work from an accredited program; prior outpatient or private practice experience preferred.
Willingness to maintain a full-time on-site schedule and engage in supervision, consultation, and continuing education.

new_jobs.description:
We are more than a health system. We are a belief system.
We believe wellness and sickness are both part of a lifelong partnership, and that everyone could use an expert guide. We work hard, care deeply and reach further to help people uncover their own power to be healthy. We inspire hope. We learn, grow, and achieve more – in our careers and in our communities.

Job Description Summary

Community Health Worker (CHW) will work with patients at OhioHealth who are identified as having non-clinical barriers to engaging in treatment plans and recommendations. The goal of the CHW is to work with the multidisciplinary team to identify barriers to the patient’s health care and coordinate support services and community based resources to address those barriers with the patient. In addition, this position provides individual consultation and follow up based on Social Determinants of Health, patient demographics and lack of resources, and coordinates support for clients.

Responsibilities And Duties

Direct patient support (60%):

Must have access to reliable transportation

Meet individually with patients (face to face or telephonic) to conduct intake interviews and identify non-clinical barriers

May include home visits or community based visits based on severity of patient risk.

Coordinate support services or community resources for patients and provide basic health promotion education.

Facilitates patients adherence to treatment plans and help access affordableMedication

Develop and track measurable and time bound goals with patient

Maintain HIPPA compliance

Communicate importance of adherence to plan of care (developed by multidisciplinary team)

Convey importance of healthy lifestyle choices (nutrition, exercise, stressmgmt.) and adverse health impacts of smoking, drinking, and drug use

Communication with health care team (20%):

Document interactions with patients and communicate regularly with Care team; Develop and maintain relationships with community resources to ensure Coordination of care for patients

Engage in multidisciplinary care team huddles

Maintain positive relationship between OhioHealth and community resources

Report how patients demeanor may impact treatment (crying, angry, etc)

Document important information ancillary to medical treatment (stressors, children, domestic violence, involvement of partner, etc)

Recognize and report signs of family violence, abuse, neglect, etc.

Administrative tasks (20%):

Maintain accurate and timely patient records.

Serve as community liaison between OhioHealth and local community agencies.

Answers phones/review messages, triages calls to determine needs and appropriate course of action

Makes, facilitates, and tracks appropriate referrals

Recognize differences in client populations and implications for identifyingAppropriate services

As a High Reliability Organization (HRO), responsibilities require focus on safety, quality and efficiency in performing job duties.

Education, Credentials, Licenses: High school diploma or equivalent, Community Health Worker Certification by an approved training program or started within 1 year of hire.

, a not-for-profit community mental health center based in Oak Ridge, TN, has an immediate opening for a Weekend
Mental Health Crisis Counselor
on weekends . The schedule will be Saturday & Sunday, 8am-8pm, with some flexibility on start/end time.

Our Mobile Crisis Team is on the job 24/7 so this position is ideal as a second job or for a stay-at-home parent wishing to maintain their skills without the commitment of a full-time job.

Are you a recent Masters level grad in Social Work, Counseling or Psychology?
We want to partner with you! We provide supervision toward licensure as an LCSW (social work) or LPC-MHSP (counseling). We pay for all required tests and the license itself. Additionally, we offer membership in your professional organization and provide a bonus upon completion of the Mandatory Prescreening Agent (MPA) program. We provide a growth environment and the resources you need to develop your career.

About the job:
Our crisis center operates 24 hours/day and 7 days/week to provide crisis assessments either in person or via telehealth from our main center location. We provide full training for you to competently conduct mental health assessments and you will have seasoned team leads available for consult throughout your tenure. Your assessments are a needed service for community members experiencing a broad range of mental health, behavioral, and/or substance abuse issues. You will be the person there when families are struggling the most.

Ridgeview
is a place where staff want to work, a place where staff are valued and appreciated, and a place where staff are proud of the impact they are making toward the improvement of people's lives. At Ridgeview, our real job satisfaction is derived from co-workers, clients, and the realization that we are part of carrying out Ridgeview's mission.

HOPE | HEALING | RECOVERY

"Where life's complexities are met with hope"

Requirements

The Mental Health Crisis Counselor
position requires a master's degree in social work, psychology, or counseling. Must possess and maintain a valid TN driver's license and a safe driving record. LMSW/ Temporary LPC license or the ability to obtain one of these licenses within a 6 month time frame is preferred in order to ensure progression to the LCSW / LPC-MHSP level. However, new graduates will be considered. The candidate will obtain Mandatory Prescreening Agent (MPA) designation upon hire or when the license is obtained; training is provided. A bonus is awarded once the MPA designation has been confirmed. Excellent verbal and written skills required. Knowledge of DSM5 criteria and ability to determine preliminary mental health diagnosis.

Provides assessment of adults experiencing a psychiatric emergency. Determines mental health crisis needs, crisis intervention, telephone consultation, linkage with community resources, and pre-screening admissions of emergency hospital commitments. Follows up to ensure appropriate service is available. Uses a telehealth system to provide some of these services in various locations. Some travel required to provide service in Ridgeview’s 5-county catchment area using a Ridgeview-provided car. Displays positive interaction and communication with community agencies and other public relations activities.

Benefits

Ridgeview offers a full line of benefits including: Medical, Dental, Vision, Retirement, Long-Term Disability, Holiday Pay, Vacation and Sick Leave, Life Insurance and Wellness Plan. Ridgeview
is an approved National Health Service Corps site. Student loan repayment for qualified behavioral health and primary healthcare providers is available.

Ridgeview is an equal opportunity employer. Ridgeview conducts Background Checks, Motor Vehicle Records, License/Degree Verification, and Drug Screens at hire. Employment is contingent upon clean drug screen, background check and driving record.

Alternate locations may be considered if candidates reside within a commuting distance from an office

Please note that per our policy on hybrid/virtual work, candidates not within a reasonable commuting distance from the posting location(s) will not be considered for employment, unless an accommodation is granted as required by law.

The LTSS Service Coordinator
is responsible for conducting service coordination functions for a defined caseload of individuals in specialized programs. In collaboration with the person supported, facilitates the Person Centered Planning process that documents the member’s preferences, needs and self-identified goals, including but not limited to conducting assessments, development of a comprehensive Person Centered Support Plan (PCSP) and backup plan, interfacing with Medical Directors and participating in interdisciplinary care rounds to support development of a fully integrated care plan, engaging the member’s circle of support and overall management of the individuals physical health (PH)/behavioral health (BH)/LTSS needs, as required by applicable state law and contract, and federal requirements.

LTSS, case management, social work or hospital discharge planning experience preferred.

new_jobs.description:
Unity Health Toronto - St. Joseph's Health Centre’s Substance Use Services provide specialized substance use assessment, treatment, and connection to internal and external community resources for patients experiencing difficulties with substance use in St. Joseph’s Emergency Department, inpatient and outpatient units. The successful candidate for the Peer Support Specialist – Substance Use Services, will be an individual with personal lived experience of addictions issues who is able to engage individuals receiving care in the Emergency Department, and/or inpatient settings. The Peer Support Specialist provides hopeful, recovery-oriented support, shares lived experience to promote wellness, and supports recovery-oriented outcomes within the Substance Use Disorder–Integrated Care Pathway (SUD-ICP) programs.

Duties & Responsibilities

Facilitates recovery by providing hope, encouragement, and supporting self-determination to individuals seeking substance use care, including those in crisis within the Emergency Department
Shares personal recovery journey and experiences to support individuals in their own recovery
Provides 1:1 support in developing personalized wellness and recovery plans, including identifying immediate needs during ED visits
Provides social, emotional, and practical support to individuals, presenting to the Emergency Department and/or inpatient units
Supports engagement and assists with de-escalation of distress using non-judgmental, recovery-oriented approaches
Collaborates with interprofessional teams, service users, and supports in the development and implementation of individualized recovery plans
Assists individuals in accessing substance use, mental health, and community supports, including navigation from ED to community services
Works to bridge the gap between service users and providers, advocating for patient needs and perspectives
Serves as a role model and provides education to staff on the lived experience perspective within ED care
Participates in care planning meetings, team huddles, and documentation in accordance with hospital standards
Participates in quality improvement, evaluation, and program development activities related to peer support services in the ED
Provides education to stakeholders regarding peer support and recovery-oriented care
Participates in ongoing professional development and networking with community peer support organizations

Qualifications

Personal lived experience of substance use issues is required
Knowledge of issues impacting individuals with substance use and concurrent challenges is required
Demonstrated ability to communicate with clients, families, service providers, and interprofessional teams
Demonstrated ability to develop helping relationships with individuals in diverse and complex situations
Ability to support individuals in crisis and use de-escalation and engagement strategies
Understanding of social determinants of health and experience working with marginalized populations
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, interprofessional Emergency Department environment
Facilitator training in WRAP, LifeRing, or similar programming preferred
Peer Support Specialist certification preferred
Relevant continuing education in addictions preferred
Recent peer support experience, preferably in healthcare or acute care settings, preferred
Excellent attendance and punctuality record

new_jobs.description:
City of Wolverhampton Council,

MASH24 Social Worker

Salary - £44,075 - £49,282 (Grade 7)

Hours - 37 hours

Contract type - 1 full time permanent

Work Style - Field: working in communities across the city

In this role, you will be responsible for applying threshold for referrals processed through the City of Wolverhampton’s front door. This includes undertaking timely and proportionate threshold decisions, analysing information, and making consistent, defensible and child‑focused decisions about thresholds and next steps.

Social workers in the MASH24 team within a 6-week rolling rota, day and night and providing a on call. Subject to the requirements of the service, and following appropriate local consultation processes, the working week of individual employees may be arranged over a 7-day period, including weekends, providing that the employees’ average core hours over a pre-determined reference period does not exceed 37 hours. The Council supports a flexible approach to working, and employees will not be required to be office‑based at all times in order to undertake the role.

In Wolverhampton, we are ambitious for our social workers. We are passionate about excellent, relational social work practice and courageous in our approach to innovation. Our leaders are visible, responsive and committed to supporting frontline practice.

We are looking for people like you – professionals who want to make a real difference to the lives of children and families and who will help us deliver high‑quality services to the most vulnerable children in our city.

At the award‑winning City of Wolverhampton Council, we work restoratively with children, young people and families, building strong relationships and meaningful connections to support lasting and sustainable change.

Our vision for Children and Young People’s Services is clear:

to develop respectful and empowering relationships with children, young people and families
to ensure children are at the centre of everything we do
to have high aspirations and high expectations for both families and professionals

We are a forward‑thinking, responsive and innovative organisation. We want our social workers to spend their time building strong relationships with families to achieve real, meaningful change. We are committed to manageable workloads, a clear and supportive development pathway, and a comprehensive training and development offer that responds directly to practice challenges. Our senior leaders are accessible and take the time to listen to frontline staff.

If you are passionate, determined and committed to excellent social work practice – and to achieving the very best outcomes for children, young people and families – we would love to hear from you. We will inspire, support and champion you to be the social worker you want to be.

Join us.

What We Offer

A strong learning and development offer, including access to Research in Practice, regular social work briefings and conferences
A clear Social Work CPD and career progression pathway
Annual reimbursement of Social Work England registration fees (for permanent social workers)
Reimbursement of Blue Light Card membership fees
Additional payments for practising Practice Educators
Supportive and flexible working arrangements, including opportunities for home working
Vibrant and active employee networks, including four staff equality forums (Race, Religion and Belief; Disability and Age; Gender, Maternity and Paternity; and LGBT+)
Access to an independent and confidential employee reporting service (“Safe Place”)
A strong commitment to staff wellbeing, work–life balance and employee support, including an employee assistance and wellbeing offer
Access to eight Strengthening Families Hubs across the city to support direct work with children and families and provide flexible touch‑down space

These posts are subject to an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. You must be registered with Social Work England and have completed the Assessed and Supported Year in Employment (ASYE) or an equivalent post‑qualifying pathway.

To find out more about working with us, please visit: www.wolvessocialworkjobs.com

Interview process

As part of the selection process, candidates will be required to complete:

a children’s panel interview
a written exercise
a formal panel interview

Written exercises will take place during the week commencing 11th August 2026.

Formal panel interviews will take place during the week commencing 18th August 2026.

Children’s panel date to be confirmed.

Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their application as soon as possible following the closing date. Please note that there are no alternative dates available for the children’s panel or formal interview.

Further vacancies may arise across Children’s Services during this recruitment campaign. Candidates deemed appointable may be offered an alternative post.

This post is subject to a satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check.

For full details of the responsibilities and requirements of this role please see the attached Job Description and Person Specification.

Should you wish to discuss this opportunity further, please contact Lyndcee McLauchlan-Brown - Lyndcee.McLauchlan-Brown@wolverhampton.gov.uk

or Ruth Richards – Ruth.Richards2@wolverhampton.gov.uk

NJC Pay Award for 2026 / 2027:

The annual pay increases for 2026/27 for NJC Local Government Employees are currently being negotiated and, once agreed, will be effective from 1 April 2026.

Our working arrangements

All council roles are allocated to either a fixed, field or flexible work style. Some roles are agile which enable and empower employees to maximise their performance and productivity, whilst maintaining a healthy work life balance. Roles with a fixed workstyle work in a fixed permanent council location. Roles with a field workstyle are usually allocated where employees are required to be out working in the community with a minimum requirement for 'touch down' space at any council location. Roles with a flexible workstyle have a flexible base location to meet the needs of the business and employees can work from a mixture of home or any council office, partner/client, or external location, as required to meet service requirements.

Please refer to the Job Description for further information on the workstyle assigned to the role you are applying for.

For more information about working for our organisation including the culture of the Council, the Council plan and vision, staff equality forums, core HR policies, employee benefits and much more please click here
.

Diversity

We are committed to building a workforce that is reflective of the diverse community we serve. We want to attract the best applications from people of all backgrounds and underrepresented groups because we strongly believe in adding value through diversity, inclusion, and equality. Our employees enable us to deliver services that are accessible, inclusive, and reflective of Wolverhampton residents.

Our status as a Disability Confident Employer showcases our commitment to people with disabilities or health conditions, advocating for their opportunities and potential.

We've received the Stonewall Gold Award, emphasising our dedication to the LGBT+ community by nurturing an inspiring, inclusive, and equal workplace.

As of March 2023, the RACE Code Quality Mark signifies our active engagement with racial equality. These recognitions validate our continuous efforts towards fostering an inclusive work environment that respects and values our diverse employees.

As part of our commitment as a Disability Confident employer, a Gold Award Armed Forces employer and our commitment to supporting care leavers - we offer a guaranteed interview as long as your application meets the essential criteria for the post.

We encourage, inspire and value an inclusive culture here at the council where employees can flourish, thrive and be themselves. We have four staff equality forums for employees to join. These help to ensure our employees have a voice, they feel empowered to speak up and where everyone is treated with respect - Learn more about the staff equality forums here

Recruitment of Ex-Offenders

We are committed to the fair treatment of all our employees, potential employees, or users of our service regardless of offending background. The Council uses the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) for any vacancies that require a DBS check to obtain information about applicants to assess their suitability for employment in positions of trust. We do not discriminate unfairly against any individual on the basis of a conviction or any other information revealed as a result of a DBS disclosure - Learn more here
